newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan says yet to set '97/98 half-year dividend.
newsitem.headline: Nissan says yet to set '97/98 half-year dividend.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it has not yet decided how much it will pay as an interim dividend for fiscal 1997/98.
Last December, Nissan president Yoshikazu Hanawa told reporters Nissan planned to resume paying an interim dividend next business year.
The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday Nissan was likely to pay a three yen interim dividend for 1997/98.
"Three yen in the Nikkei story is speculation. We have not decided yet how large the 1997/98 half-year dividend will be," a Nissan spokeswoman said.
Japan's second-biggest carmaker has made no interim dividend payment since 1992/93, but has been paying a full-year dividend of seven yen since 1993/94.

Last November, Nissan revised upward its forecast of parent current profit to 80 billion yen for the year to March 31, up from a May forecast of 70 billion yen. It posted an actual parent current profit of 32.43 billion yen last year, mainly due to a weaker yen.
